issues.note: "High manager" is not idiomatic; the usual phrases are senior or top manager.
Correction quietly changes in to at, which the note does not explain; isolate the article.
Bold for a word named as a word is correct; the quoted opening is optional.
The idiom is "promoted to manager", with no article.
"Informal" and "everyday" are compatible, not contradictory; slight overlap only.
An ordinary noun sense needs no explanation field; this point belongs in the usage note.

findings.F1: The collocation "a high manager" is unidiomatic; it should be senior manager or top manager.
findings.F2: Example uses "promoted to a manager" instead of the idiomatic "promoted to manager".
findings.F3: The learner-error correction changes the preposition as well as adding the article, so it does not isolate the error.
findings.F4: The explanation field is used for a regional usage point on an ordinary noun sense.
